title: main.tsx production fetch path is exercised by zero tests (T-014 covers a sibling entry point)
description: Iter-2 wired a real fetch path, but the wiring chosen is split across two entry points: T-014 drives `runDataLayer({manifest, rpcUrl, nowMs})` (which iterates manifest pools internally), while production drives `fetchSinglePoolStats(RPC_URL, cachedPackageId, descriptor, nowMs)` per-pool through `deps.fetchPoolStats`. The per-pool `fetchPoolStats` body is shared — that part T-014 does cover transitively via `runDataLayer`'s `Promise.allSettled` over `fetchPoolStats(...)`. BUT the main.tsx-only logic is not covered by any test: (a) the `await fetch(MANIFEST_URL)` + `response.ok` check + `parseManifest(raw, MANIFEST_URL)` chain, (b) the `cachedPackageId` mutable closure, (c) the `_origLoadManifest` wrapper that overrides `deps.loadManifest` AFTER the original assignment to populate `cachedPackageId` as a side effect, (d) the conditional `createRoot(root).render(...)` mount. A bug in any of these — wrong manifest URL, missing `await`, swapped order of wrapper assignment that leaves `cachedPackageId === ''` at first call, missing root element handling — would ship green.
impact: AC1.1 / AC1.2 acceptance is verified at the App component level (with stubbed deps) and at the data-layer level (with stubbed fetch), but the *integration glue* — main.tsx — that combines them is unverified. The most plausible production failure modes (wrong URL, broken closure ordering, undefined packageId on first call) all live in code that has zero test coverage.
recommendation: Either (a) restructure main.tsx so its content is a small `bootstrap(): AppDeps` factory exported and tested with `vi.fn()` for fetch, or (b) accept main.tsx as a thin entry shell and explicitly add an integration smoke test that mounts the full app under jsdom with a fetch spy returning a fixture manifest. Today the orchestrator is told 'all 24 tests pass' but the file the user actually loads is unobserved.

title: T-019/T-020 still tautological: App echoes stub error verbatim through <pre>
description:
Iter-1's R5-002 finding survives unchanged. T-019 stubs loadManifest to throw a string containing 'pnpm deploy-all' / 'deepbook-sandbox' and asserts the DOM matches `/deploy-all|deepbook-sandbox/i` — App.tsx renders the raw error in `
{state.error}
` (line 133), so the regex passes because the stub's own message bytes are dumped to the DOM. T-020 follows the same pattern with the per-pool fetch error: the stub throws 'sui_getObject failed: cannot reach Sui RPC at http://127.0.0.1:9000', and App.tsx renders it inside `

{msg}

` from `state.poolErrors` (line 145). In neither case does App contribute synthesized actionability text. The App-level error UI is a passthrough; the actionability lives in the loader (T-003) and in the per-pool fetcher's error messages — both of which are reasonable, but the test names overstate what is verified at the App layer.
impact: AC1.1's 'actionable inline error UI' is satisfied at the App layer only insofar as App preserves the upstream message. A refactor that strips the recipe-text synthesis from any future location (or that swaps to a wrapped error like 'Failed to load market data') would fail T-019/T-020 only because the regex was leaning on the upstream text. Iter-2 reduced the tautology slightly because parseManifest in main.tsx now generates the actionable error at the boundary the user actually hits — but the App test still uses a stub error that pre-bakes the answer.
recommendation: Lower than iter-1 reported: medium not high. The wiring fix means production now emits the recipe text from parseManifest, so the production user-visible behavior is correct even if the test is tautological. Consider this a documentation-of-tautology finding rather than an actionability gap.

title: PoolCard tests still check labels-only; iter-2 added value rendering with no value assertions
description: Tests are sealed; iter-1 R5-003 status carries forward unchanged. PoolCard.tsx renders `data.sparkline.map((p) => p.price.toFixed(4)).join(' ')` (line 55) and `fmt(value)` for each numeric stat. Neither T-015 nor T-016 asserts that '1234.56', '0.6710', or any sparkline value appears in the DOM — only that the six label patterns are present. A regression where every value rendered as the SENTINEL placeholder '—' would pass T-015 against the populated fixture (because the labels are still present in `<dt>`).
impact: AC1.3 'displays' guarantee is structurally enforced (six labels exist) but not semantically (the values may be wrong or missing). Note: iter-2 added defensive `!data.sparkline || data.sparkline.length === 0 ? SENTINEL` for sparkline (line 53), which is good — but if a future bug returned `[{timestampMs: 0, price: NaN}]`, the sparkline would render 'NaN' joined and no test would catch it.
recommendation: Tests are sealed for this cycle. File this as a coverage gap to address in a follow-up cycle: add `expect(screen.getByText('1234.56')).toBeInTheDocument()` and `expect(screen.getByText(/0\.6700/)).toBeInTheDocument()`.

title: 30s sparkline refresh implementation added in iter-2 but exercised by zero tests
description: Iter-2 added a `setInterval(REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS=20_000)` polling effect to address the contract's 'sparkline updates within thirty seconds' requirement. No test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` or otherwise advances time; no test asserts `fetchPoolStats` is called more than once after the initial mount. The 20s polling logic, the `manifestPoolsRef` ref pattern, the cleanup `clearInterval`, and the second `Promise.allSettled` block can all silently regress and ship green. Critically: the interval runs ONLY when `state.status === 'ready'` (line 92 early-return), so a bug that left state in 'loading' would silently disable polling forever, and no test would catch it.
impact: AC1.3's freshness guarantee has zero executable enforcement. A common refresh bug — wrong interval (e.g. accidentally 200_000), missing dependency in the `useEffect` array, swapped state check, missed cleanup leading to an interval leak across mounts — ships green. This was a gap in iter-1 too, but the gap was about 'no implementation, no test'; iter-2 closed half the gap (added implementation) without closing the other half (still no test).
recommendation: Tests are sealed for this cycle. Acknowledge as a coverage gap that should escalate the contract's planning of E2E coverage (E-001 was supposed to cover sparkline freshness; at least one unit/integration assertion that the interval fires would harden the per-cycle gate).

title: T-022 sentinel-marker test still satisfied by any literal mention of chain-shape.md
description: Iter-1 R5-005 unchanged. T-022 walks src/ and matches `/chain-shape\.md/i` against any file content — a doc comment alone satisfies it. types.ts now contains 'derived empirically from the capture in independent/01-market-stats/notes/chain-shape.md', which is a comment and not a derivation proof. If a developer later edits a field name to disagree with the captured shape but leaves the comment, the test still passes.
impact: AC1.6 traceability is structurally satisfied but not semantically. Low impact because AC1.6 is paired with G-PoolShape gating and end-of-cycle inspection.
recommendation: Same as iter-1: rename the test as a sentinel-marker check or strengthen by parsing chain-shape.md for backtick-quoted field names and requiring at least one cross-reference.

title: T-013 third sub-test still uses toBeGreaterThanOrEqual instead of toBe(50)
description: Iter-1 R5-006 unchanged. The third sub-test asserts `expect(result.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(50)`. The sibling `responder).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` already locks pagination behavior. The looseness is purely on result-length specificity.
impact: Low: the call-count assertion catches the most relevant bug. The looseness would silently accept an off-by-one or duplicate-collection bug producing 60 fills.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. File as low-priority strengthening.

title: T-011 sparse sparkline still does not assert values mirror input fills
description: Iter-1 R5-007 unchanged. T-011 asserts the sparkline length equals input length (3) and that each entry has finite numeric `price`. It never asserts the prices are 100, 101, 102. An implementation returning three placeholder entries with arbitrary prices would pass.

title: T-013 second sub-test still does not pin in-window result count (vacuous predicate hole)
description: Iter-1 R5-008 unchanged. The 24h-window stop sub-test asserts every returned fill is within 24h and only two pages were queried, but does NOT assert a minimum result length. An empty `result` would trivially satisfy the forEach predicate. Note iter-2's H-1 fix added a `poolId !== poolId` filter that early-skips events; this filter could (in a hypothetical future bug) silently drop everything and the test wouldn't catch it because all six in-window events in the fixture happen to have `poolId === POOL_ID`.
impact: An aggressive early-bail or over-aggressive filter would pass.

title: T-018 console-error spy may miss async errors after waitFor resolves
description: Iter-1 R5-009 unchanged. The test waits for one PoolCard, then asserts `consoleErrSpy` was never called. Iter-2 added `setInterval` polling that fires asynchronously — if the interval ever fires within the test's lifetime (it shouldn't at 20s, but jsdom + concurrent React 19 do not always honor real-time scheduling), an error from a polling fetch could log after the spy assertion. Mild risk.
impact: AC1.1's 'no console errors during initial mount and paint' is checked at one specific moment.

title: Order.price injected-event path (iter-2 production) untested; only order_id fallback decode is covered
description: Iter-2's CR-2 fix added `Order.price?` so the data layer can inject the OrderInfo event price (preferred over order_id bit-decode). marketStats.ts now branches: `o.price !== undefined ? o.price : decodeAskPrice(o.order_id)` for both asks and bids. The test fixtures in marketStats.test.ts (`makeAskOrderId`, `makeBidOrderId`, helper `order(...)`) construct Orders with ONLY `order_id` set — `price` is always undefined, so all T-005..T-008 assertions exercise the decode FALLBACK path. The injected-price path (which is what production uses, per the synthesis-notes claim that bid order_id decode is wrong against real chain ids) has zero unit-test coverage. Crucially, the data layer code (`buildPoolInnerState` in dataLayer.ts) does NOT inject an `Order.price` from any companion event — it pulls fields from `valueFields` and constructs Orders without setting `price` (lines 196-209 of dataLayer.ts). So in practice, production STILL hits the decode fallback for bids, which the synthesis notes themselves call 'wrong against real chain order_ids'. The test passes, the code is wired, but the production bid prices on real data will be wrong.
impact: AC1.4's mid-price correctness depends on bid prices being decoded correctly. The 'fix' added a code path that is neither populated nor tested. Iter-2 marks CR-2 as resolved, but no test enforces that the data layer actually populates `Order.price`, and an inspection of dataLayer.ts line 204-209 shows it does not. AC1.4's invariant `bestBid <= mid <= bestAsk` will be satisfied by garbage prices (e.g. all bids decode to 0) because the invariant doesn't pin actual values, only ordering. Real users will see wrong mid-prices on the bid side.
recommendation: Either (a) make the data layer populate `Order.price` from the OrderInfo/OrderPlaced event payload as the synthesis notes claim, AND add an integration test that asserts the data layer's resulting Order.price matches the injected event price; or (b) revert the CR-2 type addition and fix the bid decode formula, with a test fixture that uses real-chain bid order_ids.

title: Vite dev-server middleware that bridges browser to localnet.json is untested
description: Iter-2's CR-3 fix configures a Vite middleware that intercepts GET /localnet.json and reads from `~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json`. This is the entire bridge between the running dev server and the manifest the SPA loads — and it has no test. The hardcoded path resolves via `homedir()`; if the sandbox lives elsewhere, the dev server returns 404 with an actionable message. But: (a) the build path (`pnpm build` -> `dist/`) does NOT include this middleware, so a built SPA cannot find the manifest at all; (b) no test asserts the middleware mounts on the right URL prefix; (c) no test asserts the 404 fallback shape is parseable by the App's `response.ok` check (the App throws on `!response.ok`, which is fine, but the body is JSON the App does not parse, so the actionable text in the 404 body is dropped). Tests cover none of this.
impact: A regression in vite.config.ts (wrong path, broken middleware ordering, accidental removal during a config refactor) would only surface when a developer runs `pnpm dev`. No CI test catches it.
recommendation: Add a vitest spec that imports the config and verifies the middleware function shape, OR document explicitly that the dev-only bridge is not subject to the per-cycle red/green gate (which is the de facto status today).

title: App's per-pool failure sentinel-card path is not asserted at the test layer
description: Iter-2 H-4 added per-pool sentinel cards: when one pool's `fetchPoolStats` rejects, App.tsx renders a sentinel `PoolCardData` (with all values undefined and empty sparkline) for that pool while still rendering successful pools. T-020 stubs `fetchPoolStats` to throw and asserts (a) the error message appears in the DOM and (b) `document.body` exists (the React tree did not crash). It does NOT assert that a sentinel card was rendered for the failed pool. So the sentinel-card behavior — the actual H-4 fix — is untested. A regression that omitted the sentinel card (e.g. `cards: settled.filter(r => r.status === 'fulfilled').map(...)`) would still pass T-020 because the error banner would still render and the body would still exist.
impact: H-4's user-visible promise (one failed pool does not blank the dashboard) has no executable test. A future refactor that re-introduces the all-or-nothing failure mode would ship green.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. File as a coverage gap: a follow-up cycle should add a partial-failure test where one pool succeeds and one fails, asserting both `getAllByTestId('pool-card').length === 2` and that the failed card has visible sentinel placeholders.

title: T-014 fixture spy returns identical canned response for all sui_getObject calls — masks traversal-correctness bugs
description: T-014's fetch spy returns the SAME canned `sui_getObject` payload regardless of which objectId is requested — every call gets a 'leaf' PoolInner shape with empty BigVector ids ('0xfakeasks', '0xfakebids'). The test asserts URL/method shape only; it does not assert the data layer issued the right *sequence* of calls (Pool → Versioned → PoolInner field via getDynamicFields → BigVector slice), nor that the data layer correctly handles the case where the FIRST sui_getObject returns a Pool wrapper vs. a direct PoolInner. The dataLayer code branches on `'book' in fields` (line 117) and falls through differently for the two cases. The fixture exercises only the 'has book' branch; the Versioned-traversal branch (the actual production shape per the synthesis-notes) is exercised by zero tests. AC1.5's 'no indexer call' is verified, but the chain-direct shape correctness on the production branch is not.
impact: T-014's name says 'outbound HTTP shape lockdown' which it does well, but the test claims more than it delivers in the consolidated review: it does NOT verify the production traversal works against the real chain shape. A traversal bug (wrong dynamic-field key extraction, missing Versioned unwrap) would not be caught by T-014.
recommendation: Tests are sealed. Acknowledge T-014's scope is URL/method lockdown; add a separate cycle/test for the traversal correctness against a captured real-shape fixture.
